paraphrase: Consciousness, eager to manifest, projects creation (Sṛṣṭi); colours what is manifest (Raktā); withdraws its persistence (Sthitināśā); gives rise to and removes the doubt of Yama; withdraws [the object] into the fire of the self (Saṃhāra); devours even that dissolution (Mṛtyu); fixes and melts impressions (Rudra); withdraws the twelve faculties (Mārtaṇḍa); dissolves the instrument into the agent (Paramārka); dissolves the constructed agent (Kālāgnirudra); dissolves that into Mahākāla, full of 'I am all this'; and finally dissolves full consciousness into the Akula abode - that independence is the supreme Goddess.
notes: Names of the twelve Kālīs reconstructed from the verses (4.148-172) and the Kramastotra; the verses name the phases rather than list the Kālīs as a list. paraphrase: In the āṇava contemplation of the breath, seven blisses are to be recognized: one's own bliss (nijānanda) in the subject in the heart; bliss-less (nirānanda) in the void; supreme bliss (parānanda) with prāṇa toward the object; Brahman's bliss at samāna; great bliss at udāna; the bliss of consciousness at vyāna; and the bliss of the world (jagadānanda), as Śambhu[nātha] taught us.
